dossier.architecture: Tipping two-stage cascading elevator with a motorized wrist and Everybot-derived dual-piece end effector.

subsystems.intake: Separate roller contact regions for cones and cubes; retaining netting helps contain cubes.
subsystems.transfer: End effector acquires and scores directly.
subsystems.scoring: Tilting elevator plus wrist supplies the required reach and orientation.
subsystems.drivetrain: Falcon-powered SDS MK4i modules; team switched from an initial NEO implementation after control difficulties.
subsystems.endgame: Specific charge-station mechanism/sequence is not described in the retrieved interview.
subsystems.controls: Cone/cube mode selects coordinated elevator and wrist presets; driver can hold cardinal-direction heading snaps.

versions: Initial NEO swerve configuration changed to Falcons.
Complete intermediate mechanism revision history is not established.
dossier.analysis: Study as a comparatively economical way to obtain reach and orientation with an elevator that tilts as a unit. Its 2024 successor Dial is a different robot and must not be merged into this record.
limits: Some discovery lists incorrectly mix the 2024 Dial release into 2023; that source is excluded from this dossier.

context_documents.title: 2023-6329 · Two piece modes coordinate a tilted elevator and motorized wrist
context_documents.body:
# 2023-6329: Two piece modes coordinate a tilted elevator and motorized wrist

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

An Everybot-inspired gripper changes wheel orientation and adds retaining netting for cubes. A tilted elevator and wrist acquire and place directly; software coordinates mode-specific heights, wrist angles and roller directions.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source identifies containment and shared piece handling as the gripper’s purpose. Color cues indicate the selected mode; they are not themselves a vision classification result.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A shared effector needs different states for different pieces. Confusing selected cone/cube mode with sensed possession can produce the wrong approach or release even if every motor reaches its setpoint.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test mode disagreement, partial pickup and retention during tilt/wrist movement.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: 6329 presents Shock
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team reveal and reply on frame dimensions.
source_reviews.facts: Team identifies MK4i swerve, two-position tipping elevator, dual-motor intake with wrist and a 24 by 24 inch design requirement that drove layout.
source_reviews.limitations: Reveal gives architecture and packaging target. A visitor's cycle-time remark lacks an audited match sample.

source_reviews.title: 6329 interview
source_reviews.review_basis: Inherited synopsis. No fresh full-caption or visual review.
source_reviews.facts: Describes a two-stage cascade, Everybot-derived tool with different contact regions and cube-retaining netting, cone/cube presets and switch from NEO to Falcon drive.
source_reviews.limitations: Treat specific details and configuration dates as provisional.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Shock fits swerve, a tipping lift and a dual-piece tool on a chassis whose stated design requirement was a 24-inch square. The lift changes its orientation between two positions. Its wrist then adjusts the piece's local angle for acquisition and scoring. This breaks the problem into a small number of coarse reach configurations and finer tool motion. The release confirms those main mechanisms, while the contact geometry and controls below come from the retained interview synopsis.
piece_flow: Bring the wrist to the piece. The older account describes different contact regions for cones and cubes within the same tool, plus netting that helps retain cubes.
Keep possession in the gripper while selecting lift tip position, height and wrist orientation. The older account describes direct handling.
Place and release at the grid, then return to the travel or collection pose. Preserve clearance for a cone that is slightly off its nominal seat.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The compact square frame leaves less internal space for a mast pivot, actuator and cables, and gives a smaller wheel support polygon for extended work. Moving the lift from one tip position to another sweeps the carriage and tool as well as the rails. A second fixed tip position can deliver more reach without full continuous articulation, provided each position has a repeatable reference and the loaded transition fits.

subsystems.name: Tipping elevator
subsystems.construction: Reveal identifies two tip positions. Two-stage cascading construction comes from the older interview.
subsystems.operation: Tip the lift as a unit and move the carriage to height, while the wrist sets final tool angle.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team explicitly says its compact frame requirement drove design. The post does not explain the tilt mechanism choice.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The positions simplify the command space, but the structure must locate consistently under changing bending moments.
subsystems.interfaces: Mast, lift and wrist have intersecting motion envelopes. A raised piece increases the lever arm on the tipping structure.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare repeatability at both stops and after a reversal. Inspect play and test recovery from a stopped intermediate posture.
subsystems.unknowns: Tilt actuator, locking method, rail spacing and rigging.

subsystems.name: Dual-motor wrist intake
subsystems.construction: Reveal confirms dual motors and a wrist. Retaining netting and contact-region layout are inherited.
subsystems.operation: Acquire and score directly with the same tool.
subsystems.team_rationale: No contact-geometry rationale in the reveal.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A cone needs stable orientation while a cube can need containment across open spaces. Separate contact zones allow tuning each while sharing an envelope.
subsystems.interfaces: The wrist's sweep and load depend on where each piece sits. An off-center cone can also affect the mast moment.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check worn roller compression and snagging or slack in the retaining netting. Test cube retention under braking.
subsystems.unknowns: Motor assignments, current limits and grip detection.

subsystems.name: Swerve and presets
subsystems.construction: MK4i modules directly confirmed. Motor swap and heading snaps are inherited.
subsystems.operation: Older synopsis describes piece-specific lift and wrist presets with cardinal heading snaps.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older account attributes the motor change to control difficulties.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Heading snap helps only if the mast and gripper reproduce the lateral pose accurately enough for the node.
subsystems.interfaces: Approach heading and extension interact with available support and bumper clearance.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check whether changed steer behavior or wheel calibration shifts autonomous approach. Test loaded and unloaded docking separately.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact drive configuration by event and station sequence.

revisions: Team reveal describes February configuration. Older synopsis reports an initial NEO implementation and later Falcons. No complete event chronology.
transferable_principles: Use a discrete posture change when the task separates into distinct approach families and each can be reached with repeatable stops.
disconfirming_conditions: The benefit shrinks if obstacle avoidance needs many intermediate tip angles or extended-load stability sets a low chassis speed limit.
remaining_gaps: Full interview, stop geometry, loaded reach and charge-station method.
recommended_images: Seek side views of both lift positions with the same carriage height and a close-up of the separate roller regions.
